notable_claims: The Board of Regents imposed a warning policy on the University of Iowa over protests from university leadership and faculty.
Critics viewed the impetus for the policy as homophobic due to its focus on homosexuality.
classification.summary: The Iowa Board of Regents imposed a policy requiring faculty at the University of Iowa, Iowa State, and University of Northern Iowa to warn students about explicit sexual materials in courses. The move followed incidents involving homosexuality and was met with protests from the University of Iowa's president, faculty, and students. An adjunct instructor expressed concern that such policies create a 'chilly climate' for academic freedom.
classification.title: Iowa universities to *require* warnings

classification.summary: Carl M. Kadie reposted a message to the alt.censorship newsgroup. The provided text contains only the header and a note indicating it is a repost.
classification.title: Newsgroup censorship

notable_claims: CERT's recommended login banner language may be causing a widespread loss of privacy for authorized users at state universities.
The use of 'system maintenance' as a justification for monitoring can be interpreted as giving system administrators discretion to read private email.
classification.summary: Carl Kadie argues that a recommended login banner from the Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT) is being used by institutions like Salt Lake Community College and University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire to justify invasive monitoring. The discussion highlights a conflict between system security needs and the Fourth Amendment privacy rights of authorized university users. Kadie calls for CERT to retract the recommendation to prevent it from eliminating user privacy on state university systems.
classification.title: The CERT policy "virus" spreads (was Big Brother is watching!!)

notable_claims: The Florida Public Records Law was construed to cover electronic mail messages.
University e-mail may be archived for up to one year for legal compliance.
Marking an email as 'Confidential' or 'Personal' does not provide statutory protection against public records requests.
classification.summary: A user shares a warning from the University of South Florida's legal department stating that electronic mail is subject to the Florida Public Records Law. The notice indicates that the university may archive e-mail on magnetic tape for up to one year and that marking messages as 'Confidential' does not exempt them from public records requests.
classification.title: More on Florida e-mail privacy

notable_claims: An audio recording of a discussion on censorship was hosted in the CAF archive via gopher and ftp.eff.org.
classification.summary: Carl M. Kadie reports that a segment of his interview regarding censorship was broadcast on the local program 'Talking Point' on WILL-TV. He uploaded the audio portion of the interview in WAV format to the CAF archive for public access.
classification.title: On WILL-TV: local program on censorship
